articleTitle: Application of Gravitational-Benchmark Model for Road-Transport Energy Evaluation: Experimental Results and Discussions
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this study, a comprehensive justification of the practical applicability and the workability of an existing generalized criterion model was carried out. The model provides a gravity-based assessment of energy efficiency and energy benchmarking of road-transport objects. According to the model, a typical road vehicle of classification group B was tested in real road conditions, applying a common driving style. For the transport process investigated, the experimental efficiency coefficient does not exceed 0.1%, and the relative energy consumption is over 1100 relative units. A previously developed simulation model was verified. The verification shows a very high accuracy of the simulation results with an average relative error of 1.87 %. The obtained results were interpreted and, based on the interpretation, three general recommendations are formulated related to the elimination of the usage of some types of passenger cars and to the significant limitation of the application of the objects from classification group Al (goods vehicles). The passenger transport technologies should be completely rethought and gradually replaced with innovative alternatives.

articleTitle: Decision-Making Based on Fuzzy Linguistic Signatures
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Decision-making is a key process for human beings, and it is becoming more complicated in the case of uncertainty. Thus, it may be a more realistic approach to use linguistic values instead of numerical values. In the literature, there have been numerous applications for fuzzy signatures for modelling decision-making problems with uncertainty. However, there are application cases where the parameters are not measurable, and there is no way to assign precise membership values and functions to the variables. The main goal of this paper is to propose a way to make a decision about traffic related questions, using a new model for fuzzy linguistic signatures with linguistic aggregation operations in this case. Telemetric data collected by the Hungarian e-toll declaration provider are utilized for the purpose of the example. The results demonstrate the efficiency and time-saving advantages of employing fuzzy linguistic signatures over to numerical methods for decision-making.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Ensembles for Solar Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Solar power forecasting is crucial for better integration of renewable energy, grid stability and energy resources planning and allocation. In this paper, we propose a 24-hour ahead solar power forecasting system by harnessing the power of blending ensemble techniques. Our ensemble framework combines the predictive capabilities of Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) and XGBoost models as base learners, further refined by Ridge Regression meta model. We conducted extensive experiments on real-world solar power generation data, assessing the effectiveness of our ensemble methodology. The results demonstrate an improvement in forecasting results compared to individual models based on the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) score. The blending of LSTM and XGBoost models allows us to capture both the temporal dependencies and nonlinear relationships inherent in solar power generation data, while the Ridge Regression meta model was used for regularization and predictive stability. Our findings highlight the potential of ensemble techniques in advancing solar power forecasting, contributing to the reliable integration of renewable energy sources into the grid.

articleTitle: A Markov Model for a Self-Powered Green IoT Device with State-Dependent Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The growing concerns about the resource sustainability and environmental impact of deploying billions or trillions of IoT devices in the various sectors of society or economy have given rise to an energy research field known as Green-IoT (G-IoT). G-IoT emphasises the need to prioritise energy efficiency and the reduction of pollution in the IoT ecosystem. This paper presents a Markov model for a self-powered Green IoT device with state-dependent energy consumption. The model evaluates the energy performance of a self-powered Green IoT device. We derive the probability distribution of the energy content of the battery, including the probability that the energy stored in the battery is completely depleted and the density of the lifetime of the IoT device. We investigate the influence of some design parameters on the results. Introducing the threshold at which the device is forced to enter an energy-saving regime significantly increases a G-IoT device's lifetime. Apart from deploying energy-efficient mechanisms to increase the lifetime of a G-IoT device, integrating an efficient energy harvesting system into the device will increase its lifetime and reduce the frequency of battery replacement.

articleTitle: Survey on Big Data and Cloud Computing: Storage Challenges and Open Issues
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The convergence of Big data (BD) and cloud computing has considered as a prominent topic in the IT field, driven by the production of vast amounts of data from diverse sources. Cloud computing is a storage and resource management technology, reduces the cost of storage requirements. The large sets of data, commonly referred to as BD, pose significant challenges in terms of processing and analysis. This study provides a comprehensive review of the utilization of cloud computing for BD processing by introducing BD definitions, main characteristics, and classifications alongside discussions on cloud computing. The research summarizes open research issues related to the integration of BD and cloud computing.

articleTitle: Enhancing Stroke Recovery: A Sensor-Enabled Interactive Rehabilitation Glove for Improved Motor Skills and Progress Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: A stroke survivor's initial symptoms are restricted mobility, specifically hand mobility. The incorporation of remote interactive rehabilitation gloves with a game-based platform can be introduced to enhance rehabilitation quality and patient experience. The developed system is composed of sensors, machine learning, and a personalized feedback system to enhance diagnosis accuracy and promote motor recovery in individuals with hand injuries, stroke, or neurological conditions. The glove was tested and evaluated using recovery-focused exercises by participants categorized into two groups: healthy individuals and patients. The results illustrate patients' finger dexterity and agility during various stages of the game and generate medical reports to monitor areas of improvement and target subjected areas requiring intervention by medical experts to ensure patients' recovery progress.

articleTitle: Design of Decision Support Systems with Neural Networks in Biomedical Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this paper an approach is presented for the design of decision support systems with elements of Artificial Intelligence based on neural network classification of toxicological data. Precision and reliability are the top requirements of healthcare systems. The components of the DSS are discussed in detail as well as the possible workflows that will conform to current practices. The application of an $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ component as well as system improvement propositions on new data is discussed. Experimental results are provided from training and evaluation of toxicological data.

articleTitle: Analysis of Solar Radiation Estimation under Shaded Sky Conditions using Experimental Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Solar energy is a renewable energy source used in different applications that takes advantage of global and direct irradiance. In this context, the estimation of irradiance and its direct and diffuse components is essential for better energy use. In the present work, the Perrin Brichambaut approach was used to estimate the global irradiance; then, based on specific factors, the diffuse and direct irradiance were estimated. The factor for the diffuse component should be in the range of 1 to 1.5, while the factor for the direct component ought to be in the range of 0 to 1, considering that, with this approach, the normalized mean square error can be reduced up to 40% in comparison to other methods. The statistical evaluation for the proposed approach and the comparison with others has been carried out with more than 70 days of measurement in the 1-minute range through the pyranometer CMPIO Class A Kipp & Zonen installed in the city of Huancayo, Peru. The use of the proposed method allowed researchers to obtain an error rate of up to 2%. The factors for both irradiance components do not perform better if they present high variability during very cloudy sky conditions or intermittent sunny and cloudy conditions during the day. Rather, the factors should capture the irradiance variability as established in the present research.

articleTitle: Safeguarding IoT Device Deployment in Healthcare: Analysis and Strategies for Enhanced Security and Privacy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technology in healthcare, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize patient care. However, it raises serious concerns about the security and privacy of patient data. The paper thoroughly examines real-world case studies, including medical device hijacking, pacemaker recalls due to security vulnerabilities, vulnerabilities in insulin pumps, and ransomware attacks on healthcare systems, highlighting the vulnerabilities in IoT devices and their implications for patient safety and data security. The re- search underscores the urgent need for robust security measures and privacy safeguards in IoT device utilization in healthcare. Proposed strategies include strong encryption protocols, secure firmware updates, and stringent access controls for patient data. This study contributes to healthcare optimization and patient safety by addressing these security and privacy concerns, paving the way for secure IoT integration and the protection of sensitive healthcare information. Compared to other papers, its unique strength lies in its practical focus on real cases and actionable security recommendations, making it a valuable resource for healthcare stakeholders.

articleTitle: Overview and Experimental Study of Piezolectric Energy Harvesters for Roadway Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The continuous trend for transportation electrification imposes modern and innovative solutions in terms of hybridization and energy harvesting in roadway infrastructures (e.g., highways, charging points etc.). In this context, piezoelectric energy harvesters have emerged as a promising solution (combined with small battery energy storage units), for suppling low-power wireless sensor networks, traffic lights and indicators. This paper presents a literature review regarding piezoelectric energy harvesting technology, focusing on road transportation applications. Piezoelectric element types, materials and characteristics, power conversion techniques and applications are comprehensively studied and discussed. In parallel, an experimental assessment is performed in laboratory scale (emulating realistic conditions) and on the road, under realistic conditions. Experimental measurements indicate the applicability and suitability of piezoelectric energy harvesting in roadways and transportation infrastructure.

articleTitle: Methodology for Capturing Number of Pixels Calculation for Detailed Infrared Inspection of Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The needed green transition leads to decentralized production of electricity from PV systems, which means more installations in urban areas that increase the fire-risks. For better PV system performance and fire risk prevention the damaged PV panels must be detected and replaced. The diagnostics is often done by IR or EL thermography analysis that require the capturing number of pixels to be known for more precise results. In this regard, a methodology for precise calculation of the capturing number of pixels and proper camera selection, based on sensor resolution and viewing angles is presented. It is necessary in the daily practice and for training and education purposes of PV system installation specialists. The methodology consists of two main steps. The first one is rough calculations of the capturing number of pixels. The second step consists of corrections of the initial calculations for the actual horizontal and vertical viewing angles of the camera in relation to the monitored PV panel plane. The presented methodology is precise enough for most cases. The calculations for the best- and worst-case scenarios are usually enough, because all other cases are within that range. The corrections of the pixel sizes based on the viewing angles of the camera are necessary because the rough calculations, based on viewing distance only, return results with exponentially growing error for viewing angles further away from 90°. The error doesn’t depend on the viewing plane, but it depends on the viewing angle. For that reason, the vertical viewing plane is usually more critical because the vertical viewing angle for stationary installations often significantly differs from 90° and in this case, the time-consuming corrections are needed for more precise monitoring system design.

articleTitle: Enhancing Spinal Health: A Real-time IoT-based Posture Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: This study addresses the health implications of poor posture due to modern daily routines and workplaces, offering an innovative, low-cost solution based on computer vision technology. While existing posture detection methods predominantly rely on hardware-based solutions involving specialized devices, this research leverages the YOLO object detector, achieving a remarkable 96% accuracy rate in detecting proper posture. The data collection process is streamlined through LED feedback, simplifying ground truth labeling. Furthermore, this model is seamlessly integrated into a user-friendly mobile application, providing users with comprehensive posture analysis on a daily and weekly basis. These insights empower individuals to make informed decisions to enhance their overall well-being. By offering a practical and accessible approach to posture correction, this research has the potential to revolutionize the way individuals improve their health and posture.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Sorption Materials for a Hybrid Power Plant with a SOFC
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Fuel and energy complexes are the main sources of carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere. Even with the transition to alternative sources of heat and electricity production, such as solid oxide fuel cells, the relevance of capturing and utilizing carbon dioxide still remains. Currently, there is a significant focus on developing technologies for carbon dioxide capture. This is being achieved through the implementation of CC(U)S projects, which involve CO2 capturing, disposing of, and potentially utilizing. However, in numerous countries, these technologies are not thoroughly researched. The development of CC(U)S technologies for the possibility of implementation on an industrial scale is an important direction in the field of decarbonization. Therefore, the purpose of this article is to conduct laboratory experiments on the carbon dioxide capture by various absorbents. A comparative analysis for the identification of the most effective sorption materials was conducted based on the results of the experiments, which revealed that the NaOH solution exhibited the highest sorption capacity. Also, recommendations on the use of these materials on an industrial scale are given.

articleTitle: Hybrid Residual Blocks - Transformers Improving Cardiac MRI Segmentation in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is one of the primary causes of mortality and disability. By assisting in early diagnosis, segmentation techniques based on deep learning might help to lessen their severity, although extremely high levels of accuracy are required. Introduce a novel and flexible architecture that raises the bar for semantic segmentation accuracy in this study. Our contributions focus on the merging of strong self-attention mechanisms obtained from Transformer with traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. This hybrid model demonstrates improved feature representation, contextual understanding, and pixel-wise predictions, setting new standards in semantic segmentation tasks. the average dice coefficients for ACDC dataset by our model, AVG DICE 92.52%, RV 90.77%, MYO 90.00%, LV 96.2S%

articleTitle: Automated Tracking of Electrical Engineer Competencies through Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Modern educational systems in recent years combine the advantages of classical and digital education. Through them, basic and specialized preparation of students for work, development skills, and competencies in the practical application of theoretical knowledge for various positions in the industry is carried out. In parallel with this, the users of personnel (the business) impose trends related to the continuous training and improvement of the qualification and competencies (behavioral and technical) of the graduates of electrical engineering. Most often, it is carried out in the form of courses, training seminars, and workshops organized by non-governmental organizations (NGOs), companies, etc. outside the higher education system. The paper suggests a conceptual blockchain model for the automated tracking and digital accreditation of electrical engineers’ technical qualifications and competencies acquired during their academic training (tracking) and throughout their life cycle (work experience). Examples of modifying data in the system are attached. One is certifying the completion of online courses in electrical engineering and electrical machinery through shared resources from a different university than the teaching university. The other is about the possibility for students to enter data into the system when attending a conference. The examples demonstrate that blockchain technology is suitable for data reference requested by an accredited third party. These could be a funding or training structure, a ministry of education, or an employer. In this way, the authenticity of the obtained records of the acquired degrees of education and qualification is guaranteed and the professional development of electrical engineers after the completion of higher education is nonmodifyed tracked. We found that blockchain-based digital control of protected degrees and qualifications certifying competencies is a key factor in promoting self-learning and enhancing practical skills. They are the basis of successful implementation in the labor market and rapid career growth. Therefore, it is necessary to develop uniform educational standards that guarantee high quality of formal and non-formal education and its recognition by both higher education institutions and companies.

articleTitle: The Application and Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Sports Performance Improvement: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: With the rapid growth and increasing influence of new technologies and devices in sports, intelligent assessment methods, efficient planning and automatic analysis of large amounts of data have gained great importance in recent years. One of the cutting-edge technologies revolutionizing numerous industries, including the sports industry, is artificial intelligence, along with its subfields of machine learning and deep learning. Artificial intelligence can transform the way how we analyze sports and bring numerous benefits in decision support, forecasting and creating individual training plans. Athletes, coaches and sports organizations always strive for better results and finding ways to optimize training, improve performance and secure a competitive advantage. The ever-present desire to set higher goals, the increased complexity of planned tasks, and the larger volumes of data to be considered have made this task significantly more challenging. Therefore, to make progress and achieve better results, it is necessary to introduce new techniques and methods for analyzing extensive data sets, which should be capable of concluding, creating training plans, optimizing them and adapting to individual needs. This paper aims to conduct a systematic literature review on the application and impact of artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning on sports performance, focusing on various techniques and algorithms used for handling data and their benefits in achieving superior sports results.

articleTitle: An Approach for Correlation among Implementation of Integrated Software Systems, Knowledge Management and Robotic Process Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: IT innovations are enabling many businesses to update, optimize and digitalize their processes. ERP systems are the mainstay of this digital transformation. Their key aspects are customer relationship management, supply chains and human resources. With the implementation and development of ERP systems, organizations achieve efficiencies not only in the management of their business processes, but also in knowledge management. This paper contributes by presenting the interrelationship among ERP systems, knowledge management and their role as the cornerstones for digital business transformation. The advantages and consequences of implementing enterprise resource planning systems (ERP) are also pinpointed. The creation of Robotic Process Automation is considered as a natural result of the continuous development and optimization of the integrated systems themselves. In this regard digital transformation and the role of some contemporary integrated management software systems are examined in the paper. The main fields of application of these systems, their correlation among implementation of integrated software systems, knowledge management and Robotic Process Automation are presented as well.

articleTitle: Design of Microcontroller-Based Active Learning Structure in Engineering Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this work, we will present our active learning method and the tools for a microcontroller-based course in engineering domain. An active learning model based on updated Bloom taxonomy is designed. In this way, we aim to educate engineers specifically in designing purposes. A semester period is planned for the active learning model. In the course, an economical and portable microcontroller development set and programming user interface were developed for each student to use individually, which is assembled by students. In addition, training materials have been designed for the active using of this set. Each of these materials is designed for a phase of the Bloom taxonomy. The positive effect of the model developed for this course on learning is found to be close to 90% measured by the questionnaires. Microcontroller education, known to be difficult to learn, has been seen to be taught more efficiently with the developed active learning model.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Capacitor in the Distribution Grids using Dragonfly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The integration of capacitors into contemporary electric distribution grids is not merely a technical endeavor but a cornerstone for the evolution of modern power systems. This task carries undeniable importance, primarily due to the significant advantages it has on minimizing real power losses and supporting the grid’s overall resilience and stability. Guided by this imperative, the research at hand meticulously and comprehensively evaluates strategies concerning the optimal positioning and incorporation of capacitors within such complex grids. This research presents a study on the optimal placement of capacitors within electric distribution grids. To achieve this, the innovative capabilities of the Dragonfly Algorithm, a novel and promising optimization approach, is employed. The algorithm is applied to the well-established benchmark IEEE 33-bus network. Simulation and results show a notable decline in both real and reactive power losses. Additionally, there’s a tangible enhancement in the voltage profile, showcasing the method’s proficiency. For those inclined towards the technical underpinnings, it’s noteworthy to mention that the Dragonfly Algorithm-based optimization procedure has been computationally crafted and executed using the MATLAB R2022b environment

articleTitle: Cost Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations and Estimation of Payback Periods with Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: In this study, the current number of electric vehicles charging stations (EVCS) and the projected increase in their numbers for two different scenarios, as outlined in the literature, have been analyzed, taking into consideration all kinds of charging station costs, to determine their payback periods. Cost calculations and revenue projections have been conducted based on the high growth scenario for charging stations to establish their respective payback periods. Artificial neural networks (ANN) were developed using these data, and payback periods were predicted according to the medium growth scenario. An equation was formulated using the current numbers of electric vehicles and the growth rates specified in the literature to determine the number of electric vehicles in the near future. Moreover, the energy consumption of electric vehicles currently utilized in the automotive industry was identified using the data obtained. All of these data were employed in the training of artificial neural networks. The source of income covering the charging station costs is derived from electricity sales made at the stations. The calculated payback periods based on the number of charging stations per vehicle provided in the study and the forecasts made using artificial neural networks indicate that the charging station payback periods will significantly decrease in the future, warranting careful consideration of the initial costs.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Channel Estimation for Pilot-based OFDM using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: The objective of this research is to investigate state-of-the-art channel estimation techniques for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication that utilize compressed sensing (CS). The channel estimation problem for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems with pilot tones is formulated as a compressive sensing problem with sparse multipath channels. A novel algorithm called detection-based orthogonal matching pursuit (DOMP,) which extends the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm by incorporating a binary hypothesis test on the residual vector to estimate the sparsity level, is applied. The performance of DOMP is compared with OMP, compressive sampling matching pursuit (CoSaMP), and least square (LS) algorithms in terms of mean square error (MSE) and bit error rate (BER) under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios using both regular and random pilot arrangements. It has been shown by the results that compressive sensing-based methods are better than the conventional LS algorithm for MIMO-OFDM UWA communication systems.

articleTitle: The Role of Digital Platforms and Big Data Analytics as a Base for Digital Service Innovation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: Digital Service Innovation (DSI) is a new concept that aims to create a more personalized digital service for customers. DSI is a strategic decision to utilize digital technology, knowledge, and insights to improve services which has invaded all industry sectors over the last two decades. By allowing different participants to exchange ideas and develop new services, digital platforms (DP) encourage collaboration and integration. Big data analytics (BDA), on the other hand, allows for real-time decision-making and service personalization, which leads to DSI enhancement. The purpose of this paper is to have a better knowledge of the role and importance of DP and BDA in the development of DSI. The research is based on the Prizma review method, which demonstrates the advantages of a systematic review of specialized scientific and applied literature, devoted to digital service innovation. Our analysis is focused on the role of IT and specifically DP and BDA in the development of service innovation and is based on the defined by Lusch and Nambisan tripartite framework of Service Innovation The framework includes: service ecosystems, service platforms, and value cocreation. The interconnections and dependencies indicate characteristics of digital services with innovation potential, as well as the function of two of the most critical information and communication technologies necessary for DSI, BDA, and DP. The manner in which these technologies aid in the achievement of the most significant goals of digital services are highlighted, and examples from various industries are provided. In summary, DSI expands approaches to new value creation and provides a mechanism to actualize innovation by expanding the role and application of modern digital technologies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Wireless Network Distribution (5G/LTE)
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: As a result of using machine learning and deep learning in the network, we were able to more efficiently manage the allocation of network resources and the availability of the network overall. Key performance indicators are used to analyze incoming traffic and make predictions to allocate network resources to unknown devices. High load balancing and efficient use of available resources on current network portions are made possible with intelligent resource allocation. The underlying model is smart enough to determine which piece of the network is most suited for the challenge at present. 5G mobile networks, mobile communications, and the latency of modern and future wireless networks are affected by strict regulations about how long it takes for data transmission to reach its destination, dependability, how much data can be transmitted without a problem, capacity, how much data can be transmitted securely, and speed of user connection. Mobile providers are always looking for new ways to make it possible for multiple, autonomous users to share a single network. Slicing is a method that uses network fragmentation to share the same physical infrastructure among multiple networks that have competing needs. Future communication networks will need to make decisions based on data in order to keep up with the exponential rise in traffic.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power Management in Distributed Energy Systems by Considering Power Loss due to Power Conversion and Electric-vehicle Movement
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems (CIEES)
abstract: To achieve a sustainable low-carbon society and stable power supply to local areas, a self-sustaining distributed energy system” is proposed and evaluated. The system consists of multiple stand-alone small grids (“nanogrids”) that utilize renewable energy sources and multiple electric vehicles (EVs) serving as power-interchange agents among nanogrids and as means of regional mobility. Two technologies required for constructing the system were developed. The first is “nanogrid power-flow modeling” enabling quantitative evaluation including electricity loss in general nanogrid power systems including AC and DC nanogrids. The second is a “powermanagement algorithm” for multiple-electric-vehicle operations using simulated annealing in which power consumption by moving EVs is considered. Also, a simulation environment that enables quantitative evaluation of the proposed system using regional demand data was built. The performance of the system, in the case that three nanogrids were installed in Iwamizawa city, Hokkaido, was evaluated by simulation. According to the results of the simulation (performed for 365 days), as compared to the electricity loss in the case of an AC system, that in the case of a DC system was reduced by 8%. Also, in the case of the DC system, the power supply from external power grids was reduced by 33% by increasing the number of EVs. These results suggest that the higher efficiency of the DC nanogrid system makes it more suitable for regional energy supply.
